purpose: Validate evidence-obligation granularity and provenance representation on two non-acceptance pilot papers. This file is not final gold and is not used for Local EXTRACT acceptance.

papers.title: DeepCRF: Deep Learning-Enhanced CSI-Based RF Fingerprinting for Channel-Resilient WiFi Device Identification

obligations.normalized_claim: DeepCRF uses a model-inspired augmentation scheme intended to make learned micro-CSI representations less dependent on channel variation.
obligations.annotation_rationale: Central mechanism for channel-resilient representation learning.

obligations.normalized_claim: DeepCRF uses supervised contrastive learning to improve robustness of learned micro-CSI representations to noise.
obligations.annotation_rationale: Central training mechanism tied directly to noise robustness.

obligations.normalized_claim: The real-world evaluation uses CSI from 19 commercial WiFi network interface cards collected across multiple positions and environments.
obligations.annotation_rationale: Defines the scale and environmental diversity of the primary real-world evaluation.

obligations.normalized_claim: With four CSI measurements per decision, DeepCRF reports about 99.53% average accuracy across 19 NICs at seven unseen positions.
obligations.annotation_rationale: Primary quantitative result demonstrating generalization to unseen positions.

obligations.normalized_claim: The presented DeepCRF system is a closed-set identifier for a fixed device set and requires adaptation for changing device populations.
obligations.annotation_rationale: Explicitly bounds what the reported system currently solves.

obligations.normalized_claim: The paper does not establish adversarial robustness and identifies systematic adversarial evaluation and defenses as future work.

source_spans.anchor_excerpt: systematic evaluations of DeepCRF under adversarial

obligations.annotation_rationale: Important security limitation for deployment-oriented interpretation.

papers.title: Domain-Agnostic Hardware Fingerprinting-Based Device Identifier for Zero-Trust IoT Security

obligations.normalized_claim: EPS-CNN derives a double-sided envelope power-spectrum representation from received IQ signals and feeds it to a CNN for device identification.
obligations.annotation_rationale: Defines the proposed representation and classifier pipeline.

obligations.normalized_claim: The experimental testbed includes 15 Pycom devices transmitting IEEE 802.11b signals to a USRP B210 receiver.
obligations.annotation_rationale: Core hardware/protocol setup for the empirical claims.

obligations.normalized_claim: EPS-CNN maintains above-95% accuracy in a representative cross-location test where the IQ-CNN baseline falls below 30%.
obligations.annotation_rationale: Strong domain-shift result central to the paper's claim of location robustness.

obligations.normalized_claim: In cross-day testing, EPS-CNN reports roughly 92-93% accuracy and outperforms the IQ-CNN comparison.
The evaluation covers only short-term hardware aging and does not establish behavior over device lifetimes of months or years.

pilot_findings: A single paper naturally yields method, setup, result, robustness, and limitation obligations; a one-type teacher-claim list would be too narrow.
Composite support is necessary for some scientifically useful claims.
CORE versus SECONDARY importance is useful for avoiding a benchmark dominated by minor details.
Page plus short anchor is sufficient for pilot navigation; final gold still requires exact PDF hash and canonical span hash.

Pass-B protocol validation against the frozen PDFs accepted all 11 pilot obligations; one DeepCRF adversarial locator anchor was tightened to a phrase present verbatim on the frozen page without changing the normalized claim.
